CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She reports the acne is not too bad on the chest or back. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which she reports is somewhat helpful. Today is described as a good day for her acne. She denies acne flares with her menstrual periods. Her mother reports the biggest flare occurred when she started school sports in the fall due to sweating. The mother notes Kayla has been doing a good job with her facial care regimen but it has not helped as much as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Denies acne flares with menstrual periods.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No additional past medical history noted.

MEDICATIONS
Elf super clarity cleanser (evening), toner (evening), Persa-Gel (evening), occasionally Elf cleanser (morning if feeling greasy), sunscreen SPF 30 (summer)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history noted.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Household has a dog, bird, and bunnies. In 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer. Current morning routine: wipes face with water and washcloth. Evening routine: uses Elf super clarity cleanser, toner, and Persa-Gel.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules with open and closed comedones on face. Erythematous papules on face primarily on forehead, central cheeks, and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features. Regular menstrual periods for approximately two years.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate comedonal acne with small inflammatory component. Plan: (1) Morning routine: wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. (2) Evening routine: wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to areas of acne starting a few nights per week and slowly working up to nightly use; follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer and noncomedogenic moisturizer. (3) Counsel on sun protection due to retinoid use and potential for dryness or irritation. (4) Follow up in six months to assess progress.
